title: add-benchmark-lab-profiling-baselines-and-reporting-pipeline-v103
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds v103 profiling baselines and a consolidated reporting pipeline for benchmark-lab. Includes new dashboards and alert rules for regression detection. No API breaking changes.
description:
Context and motivation: This PR consolidates the next iteration (v103) of profiling baselines and reporting pipeline improvements for the benchmark-lab. Over the last quarter we've seen variance in end-to-end profiling runs caused by inconsistent payload sampling and insufficient tagging, which made regression triage slow. ENG-3421 tracked the work to standardize workload runners and add a centralized reporting pipeline so baseline metrics are reproducible and visible in dashboards.

What this change does (high-level):
- Adds a set of profiling baseline definitions (v103) for representative workload runners (chat, summarization, embeddings) with standardized input corpora and sequence length distributions.
- Introduces a new reporting pipeline component (benchmark_lab/reports/v103) that normalizes runner output, enriches with hardware metadata, and writes aggregated metrics to telemetry/elasticsearch and the benchmark dashboard.
- Adds telemetry tags (run_id, variant, quant_profile, seq_bucket) so regression alerts can be scoped to specific axes.
- Small infra improvements to the runner harness to reduce cold-start noise and stabilize measurement windows.

Commits (summary):
- 1f3d2b4: feat(benchmark-lab): add v103 profiling baselines and canonical input sets
- 7c9aef1: feat(reporter): new v103 reporting pipeline, enrich with hardware metadata and seq buckets
- 2b8a7c5: fix(runner): stabilize warmup/cooldown windows for more consistent latency baselines

Files changed (high-level):
- benchmark-lab/baselines/v103/ (new canonical input sets and YAML baseline defs)
- benchmark-lab/runners/representative_runners.py (updated sampling and warmup config)
- benchmark-lab/reports/v103/pipeline.py (new reporting pipeline and normalization logic)
- telemetry/metrics/mappings.json (added seq_bucket and quant_profile fields)
- dashboards/benchmark_lab_v103.json (dashboard panels for v103 metrics)
- ci/benchmark-lab.yaml (added pipeline job for nightly v103 runs)

Testing and CI:
- Local unit tests for normalizer and mapping logic included.
- Integration test harness added for a lightweight end-to-end run (mocked hardware metadata) to catch schema regressions.
- CI initially failed on "benchmark-lab-integration (nightly-simulator)" due to a transient data race in the runner harness; root cause fixed in 2b8a7c5 and CI rerun passed.
- Final CI: all checks green (lint, unit, integration, e2e smoke).

Review conversation (highlights):
- Diego Ramos (reviewer): "Thanks — overall looks good. Two asks: 1) can we make seq_bucket boundaries configurable by YAML so we can tune for different model families? 2) add a short note in the README about the nightly schedule and retention?"
- Author (Asha): "Addressed both: seq_bucket boundaries moved to baselines config and README updated with schedule and retention. PTAL."
- Maya Chen (perf): "The warmup window change helped reduce 99th percentile variation in my local replay — nice. Suggest adding a small comment explaining the choice of 3 warmup iterations."
- Asha: "Added comment and a link to the internal perf doc (Linear ENG-3499) that justifies the number."
- Owen Park (telemetry): "Mapping changes look safe but please coordinate with observability to ensure the new fields are added to the ingestion pipeline. I confirmed on a follow-up call that infra will accept the mapping update."
- Final approvals: Diego (approved), Maya (approved), Owen (approved).

Backwards compatibility and risk:
- No user-facing API changes. Telemetry mapping is additive; existing dashboards remain unchanged. The reporter writes to a new v103 index by default to avoid mixing historic baselines.
- The biggest risk was a flaky integration test which was resolved and annotated to prevent regression.

Operational notes and rollout plan: 
- Nightly job added to ci/benchmark-lab.yaml will run v103 every day at 02:00 UTC and publish aggregated metrics to the benchmark dashboard index.
- After merge, observability will monitor the first 3 nightly runs for schema/ingestion errors and regression alerts will be muted until we validate signal quality.

Merge details:
- Merged via squash by Diego Ramos on 2025-11-26. Merge commit message: "feat(benchmark-lab): v103 profiling baselines + reporting pipeline — ENG-3421"

Notes for follow-ups:
- ENG-3499 will track expanding v103 to include multi-variant traces and cost-per-token measurements.
- Consider adding a lightweight regression test that compares nightly v103 against a fixed golden run to detect upstream infra regressions.

Checklist: 
- [x] Baseline definitions added
- [x] Reporting pipeline implemented and tested
- [x] Telemetry mapping updated and coordinated with observability
- [x] Documentation updated (README + dashboard notes)
- [x] CI green and PR approved

If you want more details on the normalization rules or the seq_bucket boundaries I can paste the YAML here or follow up with a small RFC to the perf channel.
